source: NCERT Class XI, Statistics for Economics, Ch. 1 (Introduction).

sections.heading: 1. What is Statistics?
points: **Statistics** = the study of the **collection, organisation, presentation, analysis and interpretation of numerical data (data)**.
In the **plural** sense = numerical facts (data); in the **singular** sense = methods/science of handling data.
It helps economists understand and solve economic problems using facts and figures.

sections.heading: 2. Statistics in Economics
points: Economics studies how people use **scarce resources** to satisfy **unlimited wants**; statistics provides the **quantitative facts** for this.
Statistics helps in: **understanding economic problems, making comparisons, finding relationships, forecasting, and forming policy**.

sub: Presents facts in a definite form, simplifies complex data, facilitates comparison, helps in prediction, and aids policy formulation.
Studies only **quantitative (numerical) facts**, not qualitative (honesty, beauty).
Results are **true on average**; can be **misused** if data is faulty.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Statistics = collection, organisation, presentation, analysis, interpretation of data.
Plural sense = data (numerical facts); singular sense = methods/science.
Economic activities: consumption, production, distribution, exchange.
Functions: present facts, simplify, compare, predict, aid policy.
Limitations: only quantitative, deals with aggregates, true on average, can be misused.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Statistics studies **quantitative (numerical)** facts, not qualitative ones.
It deals with **aggregates**, not individual units.
Statistical results are **true on average** (can be misused with bad data).
